statement.excerpt: Scenario 1 is obviously dangerous, offering a tool that costs a great deal of money to provide only a little value to customers for free, meaning that at best you'll have customers that lose you money every single time they interact with the product.

from_speaker: costs a great deal of money
lose you money every single time they interact
our_interpretation: Scenario 1 concerns AI included in paid premium subscriptions without a separate AI usage charge.

Read in context, the claim concerns incremental costs from interactions before any additional subscription sales or retention benefits. The following sentence explicitly allows extra software sales to offset those costs.
A positive incremental expense is not sufficient to establish that the customer or bundled subscription is unprofitable.
The strong phrase every single time requires evidence about actual vendor costs across covered interactions, not merely a public model-provider price list.
criteria.support_condition: For the covered bundled features, each interaction creates a positive incremental vendor cost without a corresponding direct usage receipt; any stronger claim of customer losses also requires allocating subscription revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable interactions have no incremental vendor expense or their direct receipts cover that expense. Under the customer-profitability reading, attributable subscription revenue covers the relevant costs.
